  "text": "The constable pulled his boots free of the mud. “Where’s Venn?”

Mara was already at the kitchen door. The paper had blackened around her husband’s name, but the other three remained clear. She held it by one unburned corner.

“Don’t follow the footsteps,” Elias said.

“Then find me another way in.”

Ada pointed to the coal hatch beside the barrel. Elias lifted its iron cover, and cold air rose from below. One at a time they climbed down into the cellar. The constable came last, lowering the cover without letting it slam.

Across the cellar, two pairs of shoes hurried over the floorboards above them. Between each footfall came a softer sound, like someone dragging a finger along the wood.

Mara raised the key. Its glow showed Venn crouched beside the stairs, one hand clamped over his mouth. He shook his head when he saw the paper.

From upstairs, his voice called, “Mara, I’m down here.”

The man by the stairs shut his eyes.

Ada noticed a ledger lying open at his feet. Its last page held a list of names, each crossed out except three: ELIAS, ADA, MARA. Below them, in fresh ink, was VENN. The handwriting was his.

Venn took his hand from his mouth. “I thought it would stop when I wrote mine.”

The cellar door opened above them. No one descended. A pen rolled down the steps and came to rest against Ada’s shoe.

On the ledger’s next page, a blank line appeared. Then another."
